b.40b3da886f:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
b.869c7a0f72:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Isa 2:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Verbum, quod vidit Isaías, fílius Amos, super Iudam et Ierúsalem.
<n>2</n> Et erit in novíssimis diébus præparátus mons domus Dómini in vértice móntium, et elevábitur super colles; et fluent ad eum omnes gentes.
<n>3</n> Et ibunt pópuli multi, et dicent: Veníte, et ascendámus ad montem Dómini, et ad domum Dei Iacob, et docébit nos vias suas, et ambulábimus in sémitis eius: quia de Sion exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Ierúsalem.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Aspíciens a longe, ecce vídeo Dei poténtiam veniéntem, et nébulam totam terram tegéntem. Ite óbviam ei, et dícite: Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse,
* Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni, ut salvos fácias nos.
<r>℟.</r> Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Isaias
<r>Isa 2:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> The word that Isaias the son of Amos saw, concerning Juda and Jerusalem.
<n>2</n> And in the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it.
<n>3</n> And many people shall go, and say: Come and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> I look from afar, and behold I see the Power of God, coming like as a cloud to cover the land with the hosts of his People: Go ye out to meet him and say: Tell us if thou art he,
* That shalt reign over God's people Israel.
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, stir up thy strength, and come and save us.
<r>℟.</r> That shalt reign over God's people Israel.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Isa 2:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> Et iudicábit gentes, et árguet pópulos multos: et conflábunt gládios suos in vómeres, et lánceas suas in falces: non levábit gens contra gentem gládium, nec exercebúntur ultra ad prǽlium.
<n>5</n> Domus Iacob, veníte, et ambulémus in lúmine Dómini.
<n>6</n> Proiecísti enim pópulum tuum, domum Iacob: quia repléti sunt ut olim, et áugures habuérunt ut Philísthiim, et púeris aliénis adhæsérunt.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Aspiciébam in visu noctis, et ecce in núbibus cæli Fílius hóminis veniébat: et datum est ei regnum, et honor:
* Et omnis pópulus, tribus, et linguæ sérvient ei.
<r>℣.</r> Potéstas eius, potéstas ætérna, quæ non auferétur: et regnum eius, quod non corrumpétur.
<r>℟.</r> Et omnis pópulus, tribus, et linguæ sérvient ei.

<n>7</n> Their land is filled with silver and gold: and there is no end of their treasures.

<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.

b.782ea2747a:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>P</c>rídie Kaléndas Decémbris Luna secúnda. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>pud Patras, in Acháia, natális sancti Andréæ Apóstoli, qui in Thrácia et Scýthia sacrum Christi Evangélium prædicávit. Is, ab Ægéa Procónsule comprehénsus, primum in cárcere clausus est, deínde gravíssime cæsus, ad últimum suspénsus in cruce, in ea pópulum docens bíduo supervíxit; et, rogáto Dómino ne eum síneret de cruce depóni, circúmdatus est magno splendóre de cælo, et, abscedénte póstmodum lúmine, emísit spíritum.
<h>R</h>omæ pássio sanctórum Cástuli et Euprépitis.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctæ Mauræ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
<h>I</h>tem sanctæ Iustínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Constántii Confessóris, qui, fórtiter Pelagiánis resistens, ab eórum factióne pértulit multa, quæ illum sanctis Confessóribus sociárunt.
<h>A</h>pud Sántonas, in Gállia, sancti Troiáni Epíscopi, magnæ sanctitátis viri, qui, sepúltus in terris, se in cælis vívere multis virtútibus maniféstat.
<h>I</h>n Palæstína beáti Zósimi Confessóris, qui, sub Iustíno Imperatóre, sanctitáte et miráculis fuit insígnis.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.e0adb123d5:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 30th 2027, the 2nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Patrae, in the Peloponnesus, the holy Apostle Andrew. He preached the Gospel of Christ in Thrace and Scythia. He was arrested by the Proconsul Aegeas, and first imprisoned, then heavily flogged, and, lastly, crucified. He remained alive upon the cross through the second day, and taught the people. He besought the Lord not to suffer him to be taken down from the cross, and then a great light from heaven shone round about him, and when it faded away he gave up the ghost.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs Castulus and Euprepis.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy Virgin and martyr Maura.
<h>L</h>ikewise, the holy Virgin and martyr Justina.
<h>A</h>t Rome, (in the fifth century,) the holy Confessor Constantius, who manfully withstood the Pelagians, and bore much at their hands, the which contendings have gained him a place among the holy Confessors.
<h>A</h>t Saintes, (in the sixth century,) holy Trojan, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great holiness, who, albeit he be buried in the earth, yet showeth by many works of power that he is alive in heaven.
<h>I</h>n Palestine, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Zosimus, who was eminent for holiness and miracles in the time of the Emperor Justin.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.

<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.

<c>O</c>rémus.

<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
